title: CEO Interview With Nick Kurayev of ScienceSoft - Semiwiki
gist: ScienceSoft CEO Nick Kurayev argues that enterprise AI adoption in regulated sectors (healthcare, insurance, investment) is gated far more by architecture, operating-model redesign and regulation than by chips, so semiconductor progress will outrun enterprise AI transformation by potentially several years. Better chips mainly lower costs for insurers and classic asset managers, while creating genuinely new capabilities only in edge medical devices and latency-sensitive trading. Note: despite the SemiWiki/semiconductor framing, ScienceSoft is an AI software services firm, not an EDA or semiconductor company; chip commentary is a demand-side view.

themes.theme: Where better chips create new use cases

insights.claim: More efficient edge processors could let small ML models run directly on medical devices, cutting alert latency in patient monitoring, keeping sensitive data on-device or in-hospital, and preserving critical functions when connectivity is poor.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Edge AI silicon for medical devices is a direct semiconductor beneficiary of healthcare AI; watch low-power inference chip design wins in diagnostics and monitoring.

insights.claim: Healthcare's direct semiconductor dependency is in specialized hardware for diagnostics, patient monitoring and robotic surgery, while administrative uses like clinical documentation and patient communication are not compute-intensive and depend little on chip advances.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Segment healthcare AI exposure: device/imaging AI is chip-leveraged; admin/documentation AI is software-margin driven.

insights.claim: For insurers, better chips mainly change economics rather than capability: current semiconductors already support most core insurance AI workflows at very high transaction volumes, and cheaper inference will make continuous agentic operations viable at scale and for smaller insurers.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Falling inference costs broaden the insurance AI market down to smaller carriers — a TAM expansion signal for insurtech/AI vendors.

insights.claim: Kurayev expects latency-sensitive quantitative and high-frequency trading firms to be the fastest to push toward new generations of processors, memory and networking, because in trading hardware still changes what is technically possible, unlike classic asset managers for whom milliseconds matter little.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: HFT/quant firms are early adopters of new compute/networking generations — a leading demand indicator for low-latency hardware vendors.
insights.quote: in trading, hardware can still change what is technically possible.

insights.claim: From ScienceSoft's work on an early AI-based stock trading system, faster hardware not only sped trading but made it practical to automate strategies that simply would not work at slower speeds.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Hardware step-changes can unlock new strategy classes, not just speed — a reason latency-driven firms re-equip quickly.

insights.claim: Generative and agentic AI have more impact on business processes than prior AI generations because they require transforming surrounding processes rather than acting as isolated single-purpose tools.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Value capture in enterprise AI shifts toward process redesign and consulting, not just model/tool vendors.

insights.claim: Kurayev warns that assuming today's chosen AI model will perform and cost the same in three years sets a project up for failure, so architectures must allow swapping models and providers.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Enterprise buyers are designing for model-provider switching, limiting lock-in and pricing power of individual model vendors.

insights.claim: ScienceSoft's architects increasingly favor layered AI architectures in which models and agents sit in a separate environment with their own integration and orchestration layer, so core enterprise systems interact with AI without entanglement and vendors can be replaced without disruption.
insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
insights.so_what: Supports demand for orchestration/integration middleware and model-agnostic platforms over single-vendor stacks.

insights.claim: Agentic AI without operating-model redesign remains bottlenecked: an agent may assemble a case file in five minutes instead of five hours, but unchanged approvals can leave it waiting five days for manual assignment.

insights.speaker: Nick Kurayev
